finding: Actual Linux control: the runner returns typed timeout126 while the grandchild remains live. Direct-child termination is not descendant cleanup or authenticated execution-state retirement.
contract: Characterize with a real child and grandchild holding captured pipes, under an independent outer watchdog that retires only test-owned process groups.
Preserve ordinary successful command output and typed infrastructure-failure behavior.
Enforce an explicit bounded terminal/pipe-drain path for ordinary inherited process groups without introducing a scheduler, authority flag or parallel process broker.
Any cleanup budget must be declared through existing execution policy and included by canonical deadline compilation; do not silently claim the original execution timeout is a total bound.
If terminal cleanup cannot be authenticated, retain unresolved execution-state custody and yield a typed block; never declare namespace retirement or safe replay solely from a timeout.
Escaped process groups, uninterruptible kernel tasks and full adversarial process isolation require separate explicit treatment; group termination alone is not that proof.
Do not edit the live canonical candidate, kill its processes, alter maintained adopters or change workflow pins.
expected_tests: Direct-child timeout returns existing typed failure.
Inherited grandchild pipe cannot hold the runner beyond its declared composed terminal envelope.
Incomplete cleanup cannot become retired-state or replay authority.
test_watchdog: The external test watchdog is detector containment only, not a proposed product performance target or cleanup policy.
integration: Isolated characterization first. Production and integration require the complete policy/cleanup contract, affected behavioral/controls, native checks and installed parity after actual primary terminal and fresh admission.

characterization_history.hypothesis: subprocess.run timeout kills the direct child, but communicate can continue waiting on inherited pipes held by descendants. A command timeout alone does not bound the complete operation or prove cleanup.
characterization_history.disposition: The pipe-wait prediction is not established on this Linux runtime. Actual behavior returns126 and leaves a live descendant.

implementation_contract.additive_policy: default_cleanup_timeout_seconds, positive integer up to21600; explicit root/profile default60. Legacy missing value derives60 from the existing legacy headroom allowance; this is a termination safety bound, not a performance target.
implementation_contract.shared_kernel: Existing ci_graph_timeouts owns gate execution/cleanup scalar validation and deadline policy queries. Evidence contract loader/runtime and compiler/audit consume the same owner; no parallel policy registry. Preserve existing two-item gate_timeout_contract API through a wrapper.
runtime: Own each command through a new POSIX process group. Preserve successful output only after group quiescence. A normal exit with unexpected live members becomes typed infrastructure failure after cleanup.
On timeout, immediately terminate the owned group, drain/reap within the separately declared cleanup budget and authenticate ordinary group quiescence.
On unknown cleanup, raise a typed EvidenceError subtype and preserve execution-state namespace. This does not establish host-wide safe admission or escaped-process containment.
Known invalid bounds or unsupported process-group capability reject before namespace or process allocation.
implementation_contract.compilation: Quantize body timeout plus cleanup timeout plus the existing independent headroom before CI allocation; propagate the same cleanup bound into evidence contract/audit/observations.
implementation_contract.compatibility: Gate registry2.0 accepts the additive optional field; old registries remain readable under the explicit runtime default. A previously tight outer deadline can now produce an early typed block and requires ordinary canonical reconciliation. No CLI grammar or receipt family change.
residuals: Process-group containment does not prove escaped group/cgroup isolation or bounded kernel scheduling.
Unresolved host-wide admission/quarantine and complete namespace-removal elapsed bounds still require independent foundation/resource qualification.
implementation_contract.platform_qualification: First qualified backend requires Linux procfs plus POSIX wait-without-reap. Other hosts block before namespace/process allocation until their own group inventory is independently qualified; killpg(0) alone cannot distinguish an unreaped zombie leader from live work.
implementation_contract.thread_inventory: Zombie thread-group leaders do not prove their worker threads are terminal. Inventory all thread tasks in the owned ordinary group and reject/retry unstable identity populations within the existing deadline; never infer quiescence from leader state alone.
implementation_contract.interpreter_setup: Route the existing30-second selected-interpreter metadata subprocess through the same owned command boundary. Compile that setup bound and its cleanup, plus main execution and cleanup and independent headroom. This still excludes namespace/filesystem and other complete-pipeline bounds.
implementation_contract.anchor_completeness: A stable inventory still requires the unreaped leader PID and leader task in a terminal state. Empty or missing-anchor snapshots are unknown and cannot authorize success or namespace retirement.
implementation_contract.exclusive_wait_owner: Require default SIGCHLD disposition before namespace/process allocation. Ignored or custom disposition makes the exclusive unreaped-leader contract unavailable; reject before any command effect.
implementation_contract.noninterference: Owned-command terminal proof must not require a stable host-global PID population. Real unrelated process births cannot turn a completed ordinary command into a timeout or unresolved cleanup. Retain missing-anchor and zombie-thread rejection controls; do not weaken them to obtain this positive control.
implementation_contract.next_backend_review: Evaluate per-command kernel-owned child supervision using a private ephemeral Linux subreaper and waitid/waitpid ECHILD terminal proof. This is not an approved implementation or a claim of cgroup isolation. Commit the bounded ownership, interruption, setup/cleanup and unsupported-host contract before changing that backend.

owned_child_backend_contract.scope: Private ephemeral single-command Linux supervisor beneath existing evidence_execution owner. No persistent worker, scheduling broker, new public interface or receipt family.
owned_child_backend_contract.authority: Kernel parent-child relationships and exclusive waitid/waitpid determine custody. ECHILD after reaping the exact command and all adopted descendants is the terminal proof; host-global PID population stability is never required.
owned_child_backend_contract.startup: Supervisor establishes PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER and verifies it, default SIGCHLD and single-threaded exclusive waiting before allocating the command. A dedicated control/result pipe is separate from command stdout/stderr. Existing command timeout and declared cleanup budget remain explicit.
owned_child_backend_contract.execution: Preserve argv/cwd/env/stdout/stderr and ordinary return codes. A direct child exit with live adopted descendants is an infrastructure failure after bounded cleanup. Zombie thread-group leader with live worker threads is not waitable terminal and cannot yield success.
owned_child_backend_contract.cleanup: Supervisor repeatedly discovers only its kernel direct children, signals still-owned unreaped children, reaps terminal children and adopts orphaned descendants until ECHILD. Descendant forks or new sessions cannot escape ordinary child ancestry. Missing ownership information or deadline exhaustion yields typed unresolved custody; never signal unrelated children from the caller process.
owned_child_backend_contract.interruption: Caller interruption requests bounded cleanup through the same channel. Supervisor death, malformed/missing result, lost exclusive wait ownership or incomplete pipe drain retain execution-state custody. Do not substitute leader exit or process-group disappearance for terminal proof.
tests: Real foreign-process churn cannot suppress successful command completion.
Real double-fork and setsid descendants are retired before returning typed failure.
Supervisor readiness failure cannot execute the command.
Lost/malformed completion cannot retire execution state.
Fresh and upgraded private runtimes use the same canonical backend.
limits: Kernel scheduling and uninterruptible tasks may exhaust the bound and must block.
Same-UID malicious tampering with the supervisor is not a cgroup/sandbox security boundary.
Full pipeline allocation, namespace removal and host admission remain unqualified.

owned_child_backend_contract.startup_budget: Supervisor startup/readiness/command allocation consume the existing body timeout, measured from before supervisor allocation on the same monotonic clock. No additional hidden startup allowance. The separate declared cleanup budget covers interrupted cleanup and output drain.
owned_child_backend_contract.protocol: Private inherited socket carries readiness, one command request, cancellation and a single typed completion. Match supervisor PID, exact command PID and quiescent true; parent holds supervisor wait ownership until result and stdout/stderr EOF. Missing/malformed completion is unknown, even if supervisor exits0. Command close_fds prevents inheriting the private socket.
owned_child_backend_contract.oracle_migration: Replace obsolete global-inventory fault injection with missing/empty/missing-anchor kernel-completion transport controls, preserving rejection intent and real zombie-thread control. Replace foreign-birth snapshot hooks with real unrelated process births while the command runs. Never remove genuine ordinary-output or descendant controls.
owned_child_backend_contract.unstarted_commands: Preserve existing typed infrastructure126 for a missing executable or working directory. If supervisor allocation itself fails, subprocess has reaped its failed child. If command exec fails after readiness, supervisor must independently obtain ECHILD and send a distinct not-started/quiescent terminal with no command PID. Missing ordinary complete anchors still reject; a missing result never implies no allocation.
owned_child_backend_contract.installed_qualification: Reuse existing fresh/upgrade installed_consumer and isolated_python fixtures. Under -I prove bcf_governance absent, import only installed _bcf_runtime owner/helper, and run normal Unicode/nonzero plus real timeout/background/threaded/setsid/doublefork children with fixture-owned watchdog cleanup. Invalid budgets/default-SIGCHLD guard must precede effects. Exact canonical/private helper bytes must agree. No moving maintained-adopter or full train authority inferred.
